rows.ca_value: New standalone Revolving Credit Agreement dated June 13, 2025. Carnival Corporation is Lead Borrower and Carnival plc is Co-Borrower, guaranteed by Subsidiary Guarantors. Single Revolving Facility at closing, with Swingline Loans (s.2.04) and Letters of Credit (s.2.05). Further Classes (Other Incremental Revolving Loans, Extended and Replacement Revolving Facility Commitments) can be created via Increase Confirmations. rows.explanation: Both documents describe a new (not amended) senior unsecured multicurrency revolver for the same two borrowers, with swingline and LC sub-facilities, refinancing the same Existing Revolving Facility. The 'Lead Borrower' label has some operative effect: the Lead Borrower elects Interest Periods, and its rating drives the Pricing Grid (A12). The CA can also support several Classes, which the TS's single-tranche structure did not contemplate; the economics of this are covered in A05 and A06.

rows.explanation: The $1.0bn base matches. However, the CA adds a refill for voluntary commitment terminations, which can take incremental capacity above $1.0bn. It also allows a separately priced 'Other Incremental' class (the TS contemplated only additional Initial Revolving Commitments) with no pricing protection for existing lenders, and it excludes the MAE and cross-default reps from the incremental bring-down. All of these favour the borrowers. The Agent approval of new incremental lenders is a small offsetting point for the lenders.

Expiry: the earlier of one year (unless the Issuing Bank consents) and the fifth business day before final maturity. One-year auto-renewal is permitted but not beyond that date unless cash collateralized or otherwise backstopped in a manner reasonably acceptable to the Issuing Bank. Per-issuer limits are the Issuing Bank Sublimit (Schedule 1.01(b)) and Letter of Credit Commitment (Schedule 2.01), neither included in the file. Expiry: the earlier of one year (unless the Administrative Agent AND the Issuing Bank agree otherwise) and five Business Days before maturity, with auto-extension permitted. LCs may extend beyond that date only with the sole-discretion consent of both the Issuing Bank and the Administrative Agent, plus 102% cash collateral if outstanding within 30 days of maturity. Trade Letters of Credit are capped at 180 days. Barclays, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Truist entities need only issue standby LCs. Reimbursement is by 2:00 p.m. on the next Business Day after notice (s.2.05(e)).

rows.explanation: The $500m LC sublimit, the per-issuer sub-commitment concept and next-day reimbursement match. The expiry mechanics are tighter than the TS: one-year tenor overrides and post-maturity LCs also need Administrative Agent consent; post-maturity LCs need 102% cash collateral rather than any backstop acceptable to the Issuing Bank; Trade LCs are capped at 180 days; and four issuers need only issue standby LCs. The CA's $450m cap on non-Dollar LC exposure is reported under A09. Per-issuer amounts cannot be checked because the schedules are missing.

rows.ts_value: Each LC expires no later than the earlier of (a) one year after issuance, unless the applicable Issuing Bank consents, and (b) the fifth business day before final maturity. One-year LCs may auto-renew for one-year periods, but not beyond (b) unless cash collateralized or otherwise backstopped in a manner reasonably acceptable to the Issuing Bank. Drawings are reimbursed by the Borrowers on the next business day; if not, Lenders must reimburse the Issuing Bank pro rata. Each Issuing Bank has an LC sub-commitment and sole discretion above it.

One-year LCs may auto-extend for periods of up to one year (not beyond (ii)) if the Issuing Bank can block extension once every twelve months. Expiry beyond (ii) needs the Issuing Bank's and Agent's sole-discretion consent, plus cash collateral of 102% of face for any such LC outstanding or issued within 30 days of maturity. Trade LCs expire by the earlier of 180 days and five Business Days before maturity. s.2.05(d): Lenders take automatic pro rata participations. s.2.05(e): the Borrowers reimburse by 2:00 p.m. on the next Business Day after notice, with an option to finance through an ABR Borrowing; unreimbursed amounts are funded by Lenders pro rata.

The CA adds conditions the TS does not have: tenors over one year need the Administrative Agent's consent as well as the Issuing Bank's; LCs running past maturity need a fixed 102% cash collateral within 30 days of maturity instead of collateral or a backstop reasonably acceptable to the Issuing Bank; and the Issuing Bank must be able to block auto-extension each year. TS: "Carnival Corporation and Carnival plc Revolving Credit Facility - Summary of Principal Terms and Conditions" (marked "Posting Version", "Restricted - External", undated, 14 PDF pages). CA: a new standalone "Revolving Credit Agreement" (Execution Version), not an amendment. Schedule 2.01 (Commitments and Letter of Credit Commitments), Schedule 1.01(b) (Issuing Bank Sublimits) and Schedule 1.01(d) (Swingline Commitments) are missing, so per-lender commitments, per-issuer LC sublimits and swingline commitments cannot be checked.
